title: ⭐⭐ Revision: word fields, character and the trap wall

questions.prompt: Nadia spends every Saturday at the stadium and has never touched an instrument. Her sister Sarra practises the violin for two hours a day and hates football. Which sentence says how the two of them compare?

options.text: Nadia and Sarra are both bright.
Nadia is like her sister Sarra.

questions.explanation: Their two Saturdays have nothing in common, so the sentence is "Nadia is different from Sarra." "Nadia and Sarra are alike." and "Nadia is like her sister Sarra." both say that the two of them are the same, which the facts contradict, and "Nadia and Sarra are both bright." brings in an adjective that no fact here proves. English says different from somebody, and alike comes after the verb, never in front of the person.

questions.prompt: Rim writes about her neighbour: "Our new neighbour is very sympathetic: he knows everybody in the street and he makes the children laugh." Which word should she use instead of sympathetic?
questions.explanation: In English "sympathetic" means sorry for somebody who suffers, so it cannot describe a man who knows the whole street and makes the children laugh: the word Rim needs is "friendly". "Sensible" would say that he is reasonable, "sensitive" that his feelings are easily hurt, and "childish" that he behaves like a small child. The word that looks French is almost never the right one.

questions.prompt: Complete this sentence: "People think my grandfather sells his vegetables at the market. ___, he gives most of them to our neighbours."
questions.explanation: "Actually" is the word here: in English it means in fact, and it introduces the truth that corrects what people think. "At present" is the one for the time of your life, as in "At present my sister works in Monastir". "In the end" would announce a result after a long story, and "Since then" needs an earlier date to look back to.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses its adjective correctly?

options.text: My cousin is dull: she solves every puzzle in two minutes.
My neighbour is bright: he repeats the same story every week.
The book was dull: I stopped reading after twenty pages.
The lesson was bright: nobody listened to the teacher.

questions.explanation: "The book was dull: I stopped reading after twenty pages." is correct: dull means boring, and of the pair bright and dull it is dull that keeps this meaning for a thing. "My cousin is dull: she solves every puzzle in two minutes." gives the proof of somebody bright, and "My neighbour is bright: he repeats the same story every week." gives the proof of somebody dull. "The lesson was bright: nobody listened to the teacher." ends with a fact that says the opposite of its adjective. The proof and the adjective must always agree.

questions.prompt: Sonia has written a page of three paragraphs: the first is about her grandparents, the second about her two cats, and the third about the guitar she is learning. The class must now agree on one title for the whole page. Which one fits?
questions.explanation: "All about me" is the title of the whole page: it is broader than any of the eight titles of the list, and it covers the grandparents, the cats and the guitar at the same time. "My grandparents", "Pets" and "Learning and playing music" are each the title of one paragraph only, and a title for the whole page can never leave two paragraphs out.

questions.prompt: Ines is writing a paragraph with the title "Cooking". Her opening sentence is: "I cook with my mother every Friday afternoon." The third move asks for the one detail nobody else could give. Which sentence adds it?

options.text: A lot of families cook together at the weekend.
Cooking is a very useful thing to learn early.
I enjoy cooking a lot more than my brother does.
We always begin with my aunt Zohra's fish soup.

questions.explanation: "We always begin with my aunt Zohra's fish soup." is the sentence nobody else could write: a first name and a family habit belong to Ines alone. "A lot of families cook together at the weekend." and "Cooking is a very useful thing to learn early." are true of everybody, so they add nothing personal, and "I enjoy cooking a lot more than my brother does." compares two people instead of giving one fact about that Friday afternoon.
